title: Sliding-Window Streaming VLMs: Full Evaluation — Qwen3.8-27B vs Muse Glimmer 30B
summary: Qwen3.8-27B and Muse Glimmer 30B run as causal online assistants (an 8-frame sliding window plus a memory they write themselves, replayed in media time) on the Wearable AI validation split (all 2,100 sessions, with the official starter-kit protocol and, for EgoProactive, also the Pro2Bench paper protocol) and on Ego-MC-Bench (39 videos) under the Ego-MC-Bench paper's own evaluation protocol and official evaluator. Only the model's view (window plus memory) differs from each benchmark's protocol. An isolated latency study compares both models with and without reasoning.

title: Human–Device Simulation — a rigged human operating five household devices from English action sentences (3D render + MuJoCo contact)
summary: Reproducible 3D pipeline: a clothed MPFB human with IK-driven hands operates a CC BY 4.0 microwave model and a generic desktop printer in Blender; each device's key (microwave START, printer OK) is driven by MuJoCo contact against a kinematic fingertip proxy with a negative control; door, knob, bowl, paper tray and paper stack use labelled assisted grasps; the turntable, interior light, display and printed sheet are labelled motor or illustrative effects. Two recorded runs (microwave 51 s, printer 35 s) rendered from external, first-person and hand-detail cameras (preview quality). 2026-10-11: three procedural devices built from reference videos (Samsung-style microwave with 21 contact keys, Breville-style espresso machine, Frigidaire-style induction range with a touch panel), four tasks each, all rendered from three cameras; the old microwave runs stay on the page. 2026-10-12: induction range rebuilt with 4 knobs and 12 contact-tested keys; every display shows authored per-step states. 2026-10-14: a semantic action layer — parameterized action families with grounded arguments ("open the microwave door to 37 %", "set the knob controlling the rear-right zone to level 7", "move the saucepan onto the front zone on my left") — executed 14 programs of English sentences through the same pipeline; ambiguous or impossible requests are refused with a reason. Later the same day the 14 device tasks themselves were rewritten as sentence programs ("move the bowl into the microwave", "turn the dial to 2:25", "set the front-left zone to level 5", "move the tamper onto the portafilter") and re-recorded: 89/89 sentences succeeded, 26/26 key presses activated; no video on the page comes from a hand-written step list any more, and every task block starts with its sentence table (sentence · family · grounded target · normalized · achieved). 2026-10-16: the action space was made model-facing in the style of InteractiveVisualGym — one generated command list per device (the same eight families, each asset exposing only the ones it has, with its own keys, dials, parts, objects and places), a session that takes one command at a time and returns what changed or why it was refused, and five coverage runs that issued every available family of each device once: 49/49 commands accepted and succeeded, 11/11 key presses activated, 15 new videos on the Action space tab. 2026-10-18: the espresso machine became a coffee station — a hopper lid, grind dials, a three-position steam dial, a scale with a TARE key and a lift-out water tank, twelve counter props (bottomless portafilter, tamper, dosing cup, cup, glass, jug, milk carton, water pitcher, ice bucket, scoop, bean bag, knock box) tracked by a substance ledger, and two new families (pour, add); nine coffee programs (bean-to-cup, iced americano, latte, cleanup, espresso, steam milk, program, setup, coverage) were all accepted and re-recorded from three cameras, 12 of the videos new.

title: CCTV decision model — typed anomaly decisions from frames (Laya-Vision levels 1–3 vs Qwen3.8-27B)
summary: First pass at the mentor's decision-model proposal on the ETRI CCTV dataset: calibrated typed anomaly decisions (noul + choice) from frames with Laya-Vision (201M), zero-shot on single frames (Level 1) and 4-frame windows (Level 2), fine-tuned on the ETRI temporal ground truth (Level 3), against Qwen3.8-27B answering the same typed questions per frame. Two of five classes so far (abandoned_object, falling; 125 videos). Zero-shot Laya-Vision is at chance (frame AUC 0.51–0.59); 30 minutes of fine-tuning on one MIG slice brings the 1-frame model to AUC 0.73 on 41 test videos, level with Qwen3.8-27B (0.71 on its 12 videos) and ahead of it in event recall at a 1 % false-positive budget (39 % vs 25 %), at 150 ms per decision.
